facts.statement: Create an array from the supplied list or tuple fixture with import numpy as np and np.array(fixture); inspect its ndim, shape and dtype.
For a declared two-axis batch/feature contract, check a.ndim == 2 and compare a.shape[1] to the declared feature count before accepting the input.
The shape tuple gives the length of each axis, so the batch-length requirement can be checked with a.shape[0] after checking rank.
Reject a violated input requirement with a conditional raise ValueError(message), rather than continuing with an invalid array.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

practice.objective: Write your own NumPy import and parameterized validator for order fixtures with two features per order and an accepted batch length of one through three orders. Convert each list or tuple fixture into an array; assign and inspect rank, shape, dtype, dimension lengths and boolean check results. Check rank before indexing axis lengths, use arithmetic dimension comparisons, and conditionally raise ValueError for invalid inputs. Return the accepted array. Write assertions covering valid, boundary, empty and malformed fixtures, including assertions that rejected fixtures raise ValueError.
practice.success: The learner-written function accepts one-order and three-order fixtures of width two, including both list and tuple inputs. It rejects an empty fixture, a flat six-value fixture, a rank-two fixture of width one and a four-order fixture. Assertions verify accepted shapes and expected rejection without accessing a missing axis. Rank, dimension, dtype and boolean variables are inspectable; dtype is observed without selecting or converting its representation.

live_code.required_skill: Implement and test a rank-first NumPy batch/feature shape validator using parameterized Python functions, explicit conditional rejection and fixture assertions.
allowed_syntax: integer, floating-point, boolean and string literals
tuple indexing after a rank check
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide only the declared contract and order fixtures, not completed code or imports. Fixtures include [[2, 10], [4, 20], [6, 30]], ((2, 10),), [], [2, 10, 4, 20, 6, 30], [[2], [4], [6]], and [[2, 10], [4, 20], [6, 30], [2, 10]]. The learner authors the import, function, inspection variables and tests.
live_code.observable_success: In ordinary non-optimized execution, all learner-written assertions pass. Accepted arrays retain their expected batch/feature shapes. Every invalid fixture produces ValueError, including flat and empty inputs, rather than failing through premature second-axis indexing. Inspection variables expose rank, shape, dtype, integer dimensions and boolean decisions.
